Summary Collaboration Themes: This collaboration bridges advanced nonlinear state estimation and signal processing with complex bacterial physiology and host-microbe symbiosis. Mark Yeary’s expertise in Particle Filtering, Parallel Extended Kalman Filters, and adaptive signal processing provides the methodological tools to model, estimate, and predict the stochastic dynamics of Vibrio fischeri behavior within the Euprymna scolopes host. By applying robust signal processing techniques to biological data, they can enhance the resolution of multi-omics analyses, develop real-time monitoring systems for symbiotic states, and create predictive models of bacterial behavior under nitrosative stress. The synergy lies in using computational efficiency and robustness to non-Gaussian noise to unlock deeper insights into microbiome assembly, interbacterial competition, and host colonization mechanisms, moving beyond static genetic analysis to dynamic, real-time physiological understanding.
